proposition: Ibn Turka held that Ibn ʿArabī and Saʿd al-Dīn Ḥamuvayī attained the highest rank of walāya, since they alone could answer the 157 questions of Ḥakīm Tirmiẕī; the only support Melvin-Koushki cites is the Nafsat al-Maṣdūr I.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, Nafsat al-Maṣdūr I (first apology, written to the ruler judging him)
mediation.note: an apology cannot show what he held, only what he told whom

mediation.who: Melvin-Koushki, paraphrasing or translating Ibn Turka's own work
